newsitem.title: UK: Jailed Algerian rebel seriously ill - Moslem aides.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Algerian rebel seriously ill - Moslem aides.

text.p: Moslem officials said on Friday jailed Algerian Moslem rebel leader Ali Belhadj was seriously ill and they had asked Amnesty International urgently to send a medical team to Algeria to treat him.

Youcef Mouammar, head of Canada's International Moslem Foundation, and Kamel Rebeca, a representative of the Algerian community in Britain, said relatives of Belhadj told Mouammar his condition had deteriorated over the past few days.

Mouammar and Rebeca said in a statement they visited Amnesty International on Wednesday to request that the London-based human rights group urgently help send a neutral medical team to Algeria to check on Belhadj's condition and treat him.
They said that Belhadj, the vice-president of Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), had been ill for a year at a secret detention place where no-one could visit him.

A Washington-based FIS leader, Anouar Haddam, had suggested last week that Belhadj may have died in prison and urged the Algerian government to allow a neutral medical team to check on whether he was still alive.

Haddam said Algerian authorities had thrown a cloak of secrecy over the state of FIS leaders Abassi Madani and his deputy Belhadj since last year, keeping their families and supporters in the dark about their health.
Sentenced in 1991 to 12 years in prison, both were taken out of jail and put them under house arrest in 1994 in a bid to end Algeria's civil strife through dialogue.
They were believed to have been sent back to prison after the dialogue failed in July 1995.

An estimated 50,000 people have died in Algeria's war between Islamist rebels and the military-backed government since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the FIS was poised to win.
